children: Earlier this week,
Donald Trump
established a "committee of inquiry" to investigate whether Federal Reserve Governor
Lisa Cook
made false statements on mortgage documents, setting a Nov. 5 hearing on the allegations.
The panel includes the assistant to the president for economic policy, the chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and the director of the Office of Government Ethics.
Lisa Cook Can Present Evidence at Hearing
Trump’s memo says Cook should appear and can present arguments, written evidence and witness statements.
"As President, it is my job to ensure the laws are faithfully executed, including by firing subordinates who cannot be trusted to tell the truth and follow the law," Trump wrote in the memo.
On Friday, Cook’s attorneys,
Abbe Lowell
and
Norm Eisen
, said in a statement that they have "grave doubts" that the hearing is legitimate, citing
that he has already decided to fire her.
They said an objective review would find no mortgage fraud.
Supreme Court Ruling and Mortgage Fraud Allegations Explained
The dispute began in August 2025, when the

children: Cook.
Federal Housing Finance Agency Director
Bill Pulte
alleged that she had falsely listed properties in Georgia and Michigan as primary residences to secure lower mortgage rates.
In June, the Supreme Court ruled 5-4 to

params.linkText: allow her to remain in office

children: , finding that she had not been afforded sufficient due process to challenge the allegations.
After the ruling, Trump said in a June
Truth Social
post that the court sent the case back "on a strictly procedural basis" and that he would "take appropriate action immediately."
Cook denies the claims, saying she mistakenly called one of two properties a "vacation home." She has said the firing stemmed from Trump’s frustration over the pace of rate cuts.
